basis: Hair loss defines this umbrella disorder; autoimmune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Disease of the hypoglossal cranial nerve.
Pupillary dysfunction is an ocular disorder; a neurologic cause is not universal.
Growth-factor deficiency with lipodystrophy and skin disease; contractures and joint stiffness 80–99%. Atherosclerosis is a separate associated disease.
Inherited tubulointerstitial nephropathy with renal insufficiency and impaired urate excretion; hyperuricemia does not establish a separate metabolic disorder.
Cerebral palsy causing spastic paralysis of one limb; muscle weakness reflects central motor injury.
Multiple enchondromas of the clavicles and long bones define the skeletal disorder.
Defective cortisol regeneration with adrenal androgen excess; secondary hypertension is reported in 30–79%.
Organic acid metabolism disorder defined by severe epileptic encephalopathy and brain malformations; central apnea does not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Morbillivirus infection; transient rash and respiratory symptoms do not establish additional organ damage across the umbrella.
Malignant neuroendocrine neoplasm; the umbrella includes several primary sites, so a specific lung or other organ origin is not assigned.
Inherited keratinization disorder with ichthyosis and hyperkeratosis; common ocular damage is not established for this subtype.
IMPDH1-related congenital retinal dystrophy causing severe visual impairment.
Gonococcal infection commonly directly affects urethral mucosa, within the renal axis; disseminated joint and ocular disease are minority manifestations.
Hereditary Wilms tumor is a malignant embryonal neoplasm of the kidney.
Inherited optic nerve dysfunction; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis. Extraocular manifestations vary by subtype.
Defined by sensorineural hearing loss and hair, skin and iris pigmentation abnormalities; ocular albinism reported. Common neurologic damage is not established.
Prion disease causing progressive neurodegeneration; the transmissible prion mechanism supports the infectious axis.
Odontogenic epithelial tumor arising in tooth-forming tissues and involving jaw bone; dental origin and bone location define the affected axes.
Defining cerebellar malformation; polydactyly 11/11, microphthalmia 2/3 and retinal dysfunction 1/2, renal hypoplasia 1/3. Small samples limit frequency certainty.
LIG1-related immunodeficiency; multicystic kidney dysplasia in 2/5 (40%). Macrocytosis alone does not establish blood-cell dysfunction; infections are separate episodes.
Umbrella disease of the visual system; neurologic or muscular involvement is subtype-specific.
Structural narrowing of a heart valve; pulmonary refers to the valve and does not indicate lung disease.
Toxoplasma infection; cerebral and ocular disease are distinct manifestations affecting a minority across the broad infection umbrella.
Cerebellar ataxia, cataracts and myopathy define the syndrome; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism occurs in 19/21 (~90%).
